data.name: Dharmaveer
data.gender_notes: Dharmaveer is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dharmaveer signifies a hero who upholds his righteous duties and adheres to moral values. In Hindu mythology, Dharmaveer is a revered title for those who exhibit courage and commitment towards their moral obligations. The name Dharmaveer carries the meaning “Dharma (duty, righteousness) + Veer (hero, brave)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharmaveer usually hope their child will grow to embody dharma (duty, righteousness) + veer (hero, brave) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and moral righteousness.
data.etymology: Dharmaveer belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dharma (duty, righteousness) + Veer (hero, brave).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharmaveer total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_sanskrit.name: धर्मवीर
in_sanskrit.meaning: धर्म (Dharma) - law, righteousness, order वीर (Veer) - hero, brave, valiant
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: धर्मवीर (Dharmaveer) - a brave and righteous person, a hero who upholds the law

in_hindi.name: धर्मवीर
in_hindi.meaning: धर्म (Dharma) - धारणा (dharana) - to hold, to bear, to support वीर (Veer) - वीरात् (Veerat) - brave, heroic, valiant
in_hindi.long_meaning: धर्मवीर (Dharmaveer) - धारणा करनेवाला वीर (dharana karnevala veer) - a brave warrior who holds and upholds the law

in_tamil.name: தர்மவீர்
in_tamil.meaning: தர்மம் (Dharma) - அல்லது தீர்த்தம் (Thiruttam) - righteousness, morality, duty வீர் (Veer) - கோபம் (Kopam) - anger, wrath, fury அல்லது வீரம் (Veeram) - bravery, heroism, valor
in_tamil.long_meaning: தர்மவீர் (Dharmaveer) - தர்மம் உழித்த வீரம் (Dharma uzhiththa Veeram) - a brave and righteous person, a hero whose anger is righteous

data.cultural_impact: The name Dharmaveer underscores the importance of ethical living and moral values in Hindu culture. It serves as a reminder that adherence to righteousness is not just a personal obligation, but is also essential for the maintenance of harmony and balance in society. Dharmic values have been integral to the Indian subcontinent for centuries, and the title Dharmaveer adds to the rich cultural tapestry by celebrating the concept of being a hero who upholds the moral order.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Dharmaveer signifies a brave and committed soul, who is guided by a strong moral compass and a deep sense of self-discipline. A Dharmaveer is not deterred by external pressures or temptations and remains resolute in his pursuit of the spiritual path. Such a person has a profound understanding of the importance of staying true to his inner values, and in doing so, experiences the profound inner peace and fulfillment that comes from living a righteous life. The legacy of a Dharmaveer is one that inspires and uplifts future generations to strive for moral perfection and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharmaveer: One who embodies Dharma (cosmic law, moral principles) and possesses the courage and determination to uphold it, even against odds. A true spiritual warrior.

historical_references.reference: King Dharmaveer Jaisingh I of Jodhpur, also known as Maldeo, ruled from 1438 to 1488 CE. He is remembered for his fierce protection of Hindu dharma (religion) and his military prowess. The name 'Dharmaveer' signifies a warrior devoted to dharma.
historical_references.context: Hindu ruler of Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India

historical_references.reference: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, a 17th-century Maratha king and military leader, was also known as Dharmaveer. He led the Maratha resistance against the Mughal Empire and is revered as a national hero in India. The name 'Dharmaveer' reflects his dedication to upholding dharma and protecting his people and territory.
historical_references.context: Hindu king and military leader in India

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Dharmaveer' has gained modern significance in India, representing an individual who stands strong for their dharma or moral values. This concept has been popularized across various platforms including social media, the film industry, and politics. In the context of social media, Dharmaveer is a term used to describe individuals who use their online presence to spread awareness and fight for causes they believe in, often using the hashtag #Dharmaveer. In the film industry, Dharmaveer is a recurring character archetype, often depicted as a brave and righteous warrior who defends his community and values. In politics, Dharmaveer is used to describe political leaders or activists who stand firm in their beliefs and are willing to take action to defend their moral values and the greater good. The trend towards using the term Dharmaveer is reflective of a broader cultural shift towards valuing morality and righteousness in public life.
